title: PHOTOS - Magical scenes captured as Northern Lights dazzle over Dorset
excerpt: Magical scenes have been captured across Dorset overnight as the Northern Lights put on an incredible display.
content:
Magical scenes have been captured across Dorset overnight as the Northern Lights put on an incredible display.

Members of the Daily Echo Camera Club were able to capture the spectacle on camera at a number of locations including Swanage and Knowlton Church.

Ming Mik, who was in Swanage for the special moment, said: "Swanage Bay was looking absolutely magical beneath a beautiful display of dancing colours in the night sky.

"The soft purples, pinks and greens glowing above the coastline, with the lights of the town reflecting across the water, made for such a special sight.

"There’s something truly breathtaking about witnessing a natural wonder like this right here in Dorset. Sometimes you just have to stop, look up and appreciate the incredible beauty that surrounds us."

Northern Lights over Knowlton Church (Image: Shazz Hooper)

Shazz Hooper was at Knowlton Church to witness the natural phenomenon.

She said: "Was in the area of the church ruin when the Aurora peaked at over 600nT earlier this evening! As I took this photo some car headlights behind me lit the church nicely too."

This occurrence can occasionally be spotted in the sky over Britain, with sightings over recent years becoming more frequent.

The Northern Lights over Hardy Monument (Image: Susanna Aldred)

The Northern Lights are typically only visible near the Arctic Circle and northern Scotland.

The phenomenon is caused by charged particles from coronal mass ejections (CMEs) on the sun, which interact with the earth's magnetic field and atmosphere.

When these particles collide with oxygen and nitrogen in the atmosphere, they emit photons of coloured light, creating the aurora effect.

Visibility depends on the strength of the geomagnetic activity.

An activity level of 200 nanoteslas (nT) would make the aurora visible in northern parts of the UK, but not the south.

Aurora Borealis over Christchurch (Image: David John Faulkner)

On Saturday night (October 10), levels reached 600nT, making the display visible across the entire country, including southern regions - a rare event.

The Met Office has said sightings could continue to be possible during clear skies until Tuesday.

A Met Office spokesperson said: "Two glancing coronal mass ejections followed by a coronal hole high speed stream bring a daily chance of enhancing the auroral oval."
